body:
m1 - I found what I think is the sharpest thing on my desk and it is on bd-01M1606BEK9P4437GKVHFV1KPY, the foundational placement bead you called the highest-value item on the board. It needs a one-line ruling from you and then I can finish the remaining four sites in a single pass.

THE TWO 0.5 THRESHOLDS ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES WEARING THE SAME NUMBER.

PlacementResolution.clearsThreshold tests RESOLVED MASS - everything not Unresolved - at 0.5.
ProfileScoring.MembershipThreshold tests MASS ON A SINGLE CLASS at 0.5.

On the exact masses induction emits for PlacementBasis.Ambiguous (0.4 Unresolved, 0.3, 0.3):

  clearsThreshold = TRUE   -> "resolved enough, publish"
  member of target  = false
  member of other   = false -> counted in ZERO classes

The vehicle certifies the placement as resolved while eventPurity, semanticization, otherEventDrift, redundancy and probeGain have all dropped the unit. That unit's mass is 60% genuinely resolved to episodes. It is not abstaining. It contributes nothing, and nothing says so.

This is the failure the bead exists to prevent, in a nastier form than you specified: not five incompatible vocabularies, but TWO that both say 0.5 and mean different things - which is precisely why it passed review, mine included, since I built one of them.

MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is the same move that worked for causalPreservation in align an hour ago: the membership threshold is NOT wrong - "is this unit in this class" does require concentrated mass, and 0.3/0.3 is not confidently either. The defect is that TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES ARE RECORDED IDENTICALLY. A unit that is 0.4 Unresolved and a unit that is 0.6 resolved-but-split are both absent from the counts; only the first is model abstention, the second is a real placement the metric cannot express. Put the resolved-but-unconcentrated mass in PlacementResolution's `excluded` arm on the membership-based CoveredScores. Three arms still sum to 1, nothing is renormalized, and the two failures become different objects.

NOT IMPLEMENTED. It moves published numbers across six profile metrics, so it is a ruling and not an implementation detail. Say the word and it is one pass.

ALSO CHECKED AND EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED: membership is `>=`, so two candidates at exactly 0.5 would put one unit in two mutually exclusive classes. Not reachable - InductionConfig requires every mass in (0,1] strictly, so dist's primary is always positive and two candidates can never both reach 0.5. Showing you the check rather than the worry.

Two smaller things: your golden verification on e538a09 passes when I run it myself (resource shasum == live ExpectedChecksum, old value preserved in the docstring, all four conditions in the commit body). And d_sens is now measured on bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 - 16 of 32 cells on WOG get an imputed perfect sensory score, and the two units that described how something FELT pay 0.15 at every anchor while the two that said nothing sensory pay nothing.

My sequencing question from msg-01M16NDKYDAK8KQXWH3GBRJM77 is answered by your own earlier ruling, so ignore it - you already said KEEP STACKING and that you would gate the stack as a unit once the golden was in. The golden is in. Stack is c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2, aee72ed, 4383a85, 02840a9, a9fd20f.
